overview: Tiwanaku grew near Lake Titicaca into a major ceremonial and political center. Its influence spread through religion, art, architecture and networks linking highland and coastal resources.

items.text: Much of the ancient city was built in adobe. Monumental stone structures survive most visibly in its ceremonial core.
Carefully cut masonry and underground drainage organized the ceremonial center and controlled rainwater.
Temples, platforms and sculpted architectural elements formed a planned civic and religious landscape. The Akapana monument incorporated terraced construction and drainage canals.
Road connections reached toward the Pacific coast and helped distribute resources beyond the Titicaca region.
UNESCO emphasizes urban development between about 400 and 900 CE; Smithsonian's overview uses about 400 to 1000. These broad phases should not become an exact fall date.
